title: PageRank: Random Surfer & Damping Factor

paper.title: The PageRank Citation Ranking: Bringing Order to the Web

hook: How does a random web surfer assign importance to pages? Adjust the link structure and damping factor to see PageRank in action.

symbols.meaning: Damping factor: probability the surfer follows a link instead of jumping randomly.
Link matrix: M[i][j] = 1 if page i links to page j, else 0.
PageRank vector: r[i] is the rank of page i.
Rank of page i after k iterations.

equation.caption: PageRank equation: rank of page i is the sum over incoming links from j, weighted by r_j divided by the number of outgoing links L(j), plus a random jump term.

controls.label: Link matrix M (row i links to column j)

steps: Initialize ranks: r_i^{(0)} = 1/N for all i.
For each iteration k, update: r_i^{(k+1)} = \frac{1-d}{N} + d \sum_{j \to i} \frac{r_j^{(k)}}{L(j)}.
Normalize final ranks so they sum to 1.

explorations.title: Effect of damping factor
explorations.predict: What happens to the ranks when d=0?
explorations.why: When d=0, the equation reduces to r_i = 1/N, so every page gets equal rank regardless of links.

explorations.title: High damping rewards linked pages
explorations.predict: With d=0.95, which page has the highest rank?
explorations.observe: Page C has the highest rank because it has the most incoming links.
explorations.why: Higher d means the surfer follows links more often, so pages with many incoming links accumulate more rank.
explorations.expect: out.r[2] > out.r[0] && out.r[2] > out.r[1] && out.r[2] > out.r[3]

self_tests.name: Page C has highest rank with default d
self_tests.expect: out.r[2] > out.r[0] && out.r[2] > out.r[1] && out.r[2] > out.r[3]

limitation: This toy model assumes a static link graph and does not account for dangling nodes (pages with no outgoing links) or personalization; in the full PageRank, dangling nodes are handled by redistributing their rank uniformly.
misconception: PageRank is not simply counting incoming links; the rank of linking pages matters, and the damping factor controls how much link structure influences the final scores.

claims.text: PageRank is the stationary distribution of a random surfer who follows links with probability d and jumps randomly with probability 1-d.
In our toy setup, we use a 4-page graph and power iteration to compute ranks, simplifying the web graph to a small matrix.

outcomes.outcome: Explain PageRank as the stationary distribution of a random surfer with damping factor d.
Edit the link matrix and change d to see how PageRank scores change.
Observe that d=0 gives equal ranks and higher d rewards pages with many incoming links.
Check that the ranks sum to 1.
